comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 lists nine compulsory components totaling 60 EC, including four successive Modern Greek language-acquisition courses, Byzantine and modern Greek history, humanities and regional-studies foundations, and Project Athens. Year 2 contains five 6-EC UvA courses in advanced Greek language and literature, national identity, conflict and cultural history, followed by the required half-year study-abroad semester in Greece or Cyprus. The compact table labels the administrative Buitenlandverblijf component as 6 EC, while the accompanying text identifies the whole second semester as the abroad period and expects 12 EC of Modern Greek language acquisition there; the 30-EC semester is therefore preserved as one integrated abroad block without inventing host courses. Year 3 lists three 6-EC Mediterranean and Greece-Europe courses, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC thesis. This yields the coherent published 60+60+60 pathway.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum requires four successive Modern Greek language-acquisition courses in year 1, two advanced Modern Greek language-and-literature courses in year 2, further Greek-language acquisition during a required semester in Greece or Cyprus, Greek-language source use, and a Modern Greek subject thesis. This language progression is integrated with Byzantine legacies, modern Greek and Cypriot history, Greece-Turkey-Cyprus conflict and memory, Greek-European relations and contemporary Mediterranean culture. The current UCR catalogue has no Modern Greek language instruction, Greek grammar or translation, or advanced Greek-language reading and writing sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from ancient Greek archaeology, general literature, history, politics, philosophy and Mediterranean art would replace the programme's compulsory modern-language and area-studies core rather than provide a defensible closest match. The 30 EC of genuine open choice cannot compensate for the missing compulsory Modern Greek sequence and country-specific progression.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected full-time pathway totals exactly 180 EC: a 60-EC first year, 30 EC of listed second-year UvA courses plus a required 30-EC half-year abroad semester, and a third year with 18 EC compulsory regional study, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC thesis. The public page's compact table displays a 6-EC administrative Buitenlandverblijf entry, but its explanatory text defines the whole second semester as study in Greece or Cyprus and expects 12 EC of Greek language acquisition during that period. Representing the semester as one 30-EC block preserves the published year total and avoids inventing host-university courses. The exception rests on the missing Modern Greek disciplinary core, not on this presentation discrepancy.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned terms and topics. MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology focuses on community and democracy in early-democratic ancient Greece; MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy examines Athenian democracy, archaeology and heritage; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature includes ancient Greek and Byzantine narrative among a global set; GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy begins with ancient Greek philosophy; and GOSHIST213 Western Way of War ranges from Greek hoplites to the modern era. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean, GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations and GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict provide broader historical, Mediterranean or political context. These courses concern antiquity, general regional history or adjacent methods. None teaches Modern Greek grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, speaking, writing, translation or Greek-language source analysis, and none provides a sustained modern Greece/Cyprus area-studies sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Modern Greek Language and Culture programme.
